text:
In a large classroom, there was a boy named Adam who never spoke. He sat in the last row and looked at his desk. Some students laughed at him, and others simply forgot that he existed.

His teacher, Mrs. Lopez, noticed him. She didn’t force him to speak. Instead, she began to write small comments on his homework: “This is a clever idea.” “I like the way you think.” “I’d love to hear more about this.”

At first, Adam didn’t react. But after a few weeks, he started to write longer answers. After a few months, he began to raise his hand, only once or twice, and very quietly.

One day, the class was discussing a difficult poem. Nobody understood it. Mrs. Lopez looked at Adam, and he spoke clearly for the first time. His interpretation was so thoughtful that the whole room fell silent.

At the end of the school year, Adam wrote a letter to his teacher. “Thank you for seeing me,” he wrote. “I thought that nobody would care what I think. You showed me that my voice mattered.”

Mrs. Lopez kept the letter in her desk for the rest of her career. When she felt tired or discouraged, she took it out and read it again.

Moral: Sometimes a small word of encouragement can open a person’s whole future.

Mrs. Lopez forced Adam to speak in class.
How did Mrs. Lopez help Adam?
o: She wrote small encouraging comments on his homework
